ANC-1.1.title: : Antenatal Registration and Scheduling
ANC-1.1.raw_text: Every pregnant woman should be registered within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. Four standard antenatal visits are scheduled to monitor maternal health, fetal growth, and blood pressure.
ANC-1.1.clean_text: Every pregnant woman should be registered within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. Four standard antenatal visits are scheduled to monitor maternal health, fetal growth, and blood pressure.

ANC-1.2.title: : Nutritional Care and Iron Folic Acid
ANC-1.2.full_title: : Nutritional Care and Iron Folic Acid
ANC-1.2.raw_text: Administer 180 tablets of Iron Folic Acid (IFA) starting from the second trimester to prevent maternal anaemia. Advise a balanced diet with green leafy vegetables and dairy.
ANC-1.2.clean_text: Administer 180 tablets of Iron Folic Acid (IFA) starting from the second trimester to prevent maternal anaemia. Advise a balanced diet with green leafy vegetables and dairy.

ANC-1.3.title: : Identification of High Risk Pregnancy
ANC-1.3.raw_text: Identify high-risk factors including severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dL), pre-eclampsia (BP >= 140/90 with proteinuria), previous Caesarean section, and maternal age under 18 or over 35.
ANC-1.3.clean_text: Identify high-risk factors including severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dL), pre-eclampsia (BP >= 140/90 with proteinuria), previous Caesarean section, and maternal age under 18 or over 35.

IMM-1.1.title: : Primary Vaccination Schedule
IMM-1.1.raw_text: Newborns receive BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B at birth. Pentavalent-1 and Rota-1 are administered at 6 weeks of age.
IMM-1.1.clean_text: Newborns receive BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B at birth. Pentavalent-1 and Rota-1 are administered at 6 weeks of age.

CHD-1.1.title: : Management of Diarrhoea and Dehydration
CHD-1.1.raw_text: Administer Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and Zinc dispersible tablets (20 mg daily for 14 days) to prevent severe dehydration during acute watery diarrhoea.
CHD-1.1.clean_text: Administer Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and Zinc dispersible tablets (20 mg daily for 14 days) to prevent severe dehydration during acute watery diarrhoea.

NUT-1.1.title: : Malnutrition Screening via MUAC
NUT-1.1.raw_text: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) color bands indicate nutritional status: Red (< 11.5 cm) indicates Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), Yellow (11.5 - 12.5 cm) indicates Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), and Green (> 12.5 cm) indicates Normal nutrition.
NUT-1.1.clean_text: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) color bands indicate nutritional status: Red (< 11.5 cm) indicates Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), Yellow (11.5 - 12.5 cm) indicates Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), and Green (> 12.5 cm) indicates Normal nutrition.

ESC-1.1.title: : Severe Obstetric Danger Signs
ESC-1.1.raw_text: Immediate ambulance transfer (108/102) is required for heavy vaginal bleeding, convulsions or seizures, severe persistent headache with blurred vision, and high fever during pregnancy or labour.
ESC-1.1.clean_text: Immediate ambulance transfer (108/102) is required for heavy vaginal bleeding, convulsions or seizures, severe persistent headache with blurred vision, and high fever during pregnancy or labour.

ESC-2.1.title: : Neonatal Red Flags
ESC-2.1.raw_text: Transfer urgently if the infant is cold to touch despite skin-to-skin contact, has chest indrawing or grunting, is unable to feed, or presents with yellow soles and palms (severe jaundice).
ESC-2.1.clean_text: Transfer urgently if the infant is cold to touch despite skin-to-skin contact, has chest indrawing or grunting, is unable to feed, or presents with yellow soles and palms (severe jaundice).

SCP-1.1.title: : Scope Boundaries and Medical Officer Referral
SCP-1.1.full_title: : Scope Boundaries and Medical Officer Referral
SCP-1.1.raw_text: Frontline workers do not prescribe antibiotics or injectables. If high-grade fever persists beyond 48 hours or suspected bacterial infection occurs, immediately refer to the Medical Officer at the Primary Health Centre.
